Weekly Discussion: Will Voat be able to avoid the same fate as Reddit?

Depends.

History has shown us that nothing man made has ever/will last forever.

I think it depends on the admins and how far there willing to allow free speech and true discussion without the reddit circlejerk.

I came over here personally to start anew from what reddit has become the last few years.

I am personally skeptical that Voat will ever attain a level of population or activity anywhere near Reddit's in the first place. The average Redditor doesn't much care about the corruption or hypocrisy of higher-ups, so they have no real reason to leave unless we see some kind of mass expulsion attempt by Reddit admins of "political undesirables". Voat simply doesn't offer anything new and exciting to draw people in.

However I believe that as people become more conscious of and invested in the political actions of the websites they enjoy, I believe Reddit's eventual replacement (and there will be one) will have an interest in preserving the support of anti-censorship and anti-corruption watchdogs. We will see new websites adhering to Voat's general philosophy.

Most importantly though is that we don't have extensive information on the administration team behind Voat. What the establishment of this website has shown however is that places like it are dispensable: this population is not at all similar to the population of the more "mainstream" reddit; we will be quick to abandon this place and establish another clone because there is, again, very little draw to Voat besides it's politics.

Probably not. It has happened before and it will eventually happen again. Just as people left Digg for Reddit, and as people leave Reddit for Voat, one day we will get too big and the cycle will continue. But for now I say that we just enjoy our safe haven here at Voat before the inevitable does happen.

Perhaps Voat will never become the next Reddit though. How many social media sites have risen and disappeared without us even noticing? Voat could remain a small social network if we/its caretakers want it to be.
Even if we do manage to keep it small, what's to say it wont eventually turn sour? I'd imagine that we might at least get bored with it after many years.
But it's not because it stays small that the community stays the same. As long as the amount of people joining only exceeds the amount leaving by a little bit the community could stay healthy?

But if the community is being replaced at a constant rate, then wouldn't it be completely different one day? Who's to say that the culture wouldn't be completely changed by then? Oh well, these are just ideas. Personally I hope we can maintain our site to the current standard for as long as possible, I don't really fancy migrating again.
Yes of course, no different with real life society. Maybe in 5 years time you won't even have a need for a community like this anymore, so who knows. Or new media will emerge!
That's true, five years certainly is a long time in terms of the current rate of development of technology. Who knows what people will be doing then? It's exciting to think about really.

  2. the left branch has more variability in position
